newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian reserves rise to 31 trln rbls June 1.
newsitem.headline: Russian reserves rise to 31 trln rbls June 1.

text.p: Russia's net international reserves rose to about 31 trillion roubles on June 1 from 23.5 trillion on May 1, Central Bank First Deputy Chairman Sergei Aleksashenko said on Monday.

Gross reserves are currently around $19 billion, he told a news conference. Reserves this year are calculated at a rate of 5,560 roubles to the dollar, against a current trading level of about 5,770 to the dollar, taking current net reserves to $5.6 billion.

Net international reserves are the reserves of the central bank and government excluding loans from the International Monetary Fund and other liabilities up to one year. Central bank officials say reserves have been growing this year because of purchases of dollars in the currency market.

"The growth trend of Central Bank currency reserves is not causing danger. We expected this and we are trying to issue the roubles called for by our dollar purchases in regular doses, and to keep them under control," Aleksashenko said.

Aleksashenko said the Central Bank was not yet sated with dollars. Nor would it sell dollars to cause a sharp fall in the dollar against the rouble, as this would hurt both exporters and ordinary people, many of whom hold savings in cash dollars.

Aleksashenko said the authorities would stick next year to the current predictable currency policy of a gradual depreciation in the rouble, with the rouble depreciating at a slightly slower rate than inflation. But they have not yet decided technically whether to achieve this with the present system of currency bands, known as a sloping corridor, or use some other system, he said.
